comparison.warmup: Which One Doesn't Belong four food/sandwich images; learner should discuss features and fairness; source images not copied
comparison.activity1: Choose distinct values from 2, 3, 5 for sandwich count and person count; draw equal sharing and explain why total amounts, not merely piece counts, are equal
comparison.activity2: Han's pictured two-sandwich, three-person model; one sandwich divided into two halves, other sandwich one half for person 3 plus three equal one-sixth portions, yielding 1/2+1/6=2/3 per person. Students must make a DIFFERENT valid partition drawing.
comparison.didacticPrecision: This introductory lesson deliberately does NOT require formal symbolic division equations or formal naming of every fraction; source prioritizes diagrams, explanations and discussion.
comparison.candidate: Current Grade-5-owned Rich V2 U02:L01 sidecar matches exploration, informal 2/3 and 3/2 sharing, alternate equal-amount models and teacher-scored reasoning; its third worked example 1/2+1/6=2/3 is mathematically consistent with the teacher HTML description of Han's partition.
comparison.verificationMath: Three recipients × (1/2+1/6)=2 identical sandwiches; six 1/3 parts also give two thirds per recipient. Equal fragment counts alone do not prove equal whole amounts.
comparison.remainingGaps: No authentic Student Task PDF screenshot/figure parity, no independently checked individual publisher image licensing, no actual selected Practice family, real source drawing rubric, authenticated B/D, saved work, two-tenant isolation, owner UAT or production proof.
comparison.changeDisposition: Keep existing candidate without duplicating or forcing symbolic-quotient pedagogy; track separate PDF and teacher-drawing gates.

teacherRubric.mustCheck: Same-sized sandwich wholes; exactly two source sandwiches; three recipients of equal total food; at least two different diagrammatic constructions; reasoning understandable to peers.
teacherRubric.mustReject: Assuming equal piece count guarantees equal area/amount, more than two sandwiches in total, or accepting numerical 2/3 without a source-required student representation.
